svg.title: AI engineering tools across six SDLC stages
svg.desc: Six stage panels compare nine tools, their documented features, and source-assessed capability depth. M1 task assistance, M2 repeatable workflow, M3 maintained context. External and unestablished deployment coverage are shown explicitly. These are not verified product maturity ratings.
svg.text: Analysis → Design → Implementation → QA → Deployment → Maintenance → feedback
Maturity here = documented capability depth per stage, not reliability, market adoption or a tool ranking.
M3 includes durable constraints, records or feedback that inform later work. It does not mean autonomous or fully enforced.
Clarify supplied intent and acceptance criteria
Product brief, PRD and requirement identities
Clarify problem and approve change scope
Clarify intent; create specs and tickets
Evaluate options; govern HLD and solution
Shared architecture spine and decision IDs
Plan decisions using prior solution knowledge
Change design linked to current system specs
Inject shared standards into shaped specs
Domain model, context map and ADRs
Layer agents, HLD constraints, step approvals
Story delivery under shared project context
Task agents, TDD and spec/quality reviews
Planned delivery informed by reusable lessons
Apply change tasks against system specs
Implement tickets with TDD and review
Execute spec tasks using project steering
Checks, deviation ledger and quality statistics
Analyze consistency; converge code with spec
Standards inform checks owned by host
Infra work/evidence; no general release engine
Branch/PR handoff is not production rollout
Not established by reviewed spec/steering docs
History, drift checks, Evolve and patch recipes
Refresh context and shared architectural records
Capture solutions; retrieve lessons next time
Archive changes; merge into current specs
Maintain specs and persistent project steering
Analysis: technical clarification ≠ product discovery. QA: review ≠ complete security/performance assurance.
Maintenance: engineering knowledge ≠ production monitoring or incident response. Deployment gaps are intentional evidence gaps.
Source assessment • 17 September 2026 • See the accompanying coverage table, competitor sources and Artisyn capability audit.
